    Adapted from user's Option C2 (originally QS Top 100 universities 2025) after Wikipedia

    70% / etc. Pivoted to Fields Medal seed: "Which countries have produced more than 5
    Fields Medal winners?" — same comparator phrasing, full Wikipedia coverage.

    Schema: Country (key) | Fields Medalists (numeric) | Qualifies (>5) (categorical Yes/No) |
    Example Medalists (text, semicolon-delimited).

    query_category: comparative (NEW for benchmark — fills the 0/5 gap)
    secondary_category: aggregation
    operation_type: aggregation
    claim_type: source_defined
    domain: Science/Mathematics

    7 Wikipedia source URLs: 1 master Fields Medal article + 6 per-medalist articles for
    dual-nationality validation (Yau, Deligne, Drinfeld, Birkar, Huh, Grothendieck).

    Per-country tally (1936-2022, total 64 medalists matching Wikipedia article aggregate):

    - Japan: 3 (No)
    - Australia/Belgium/Germany/Iran/Italy/Ukraine: 2 each (No)
    - Brazil/Finland/Hong Kong/Israel/New Zealand/Norway/Sweden/Vietnam: 1 each (No)

    Counting rule (deterministic): each medalist counts toward exactly ONE country = first
    listed nationality in the Fields Medal article. For Soviet-era medalists with secondary
    nationality (e.g., "Soviet Union/Russia", "Soviet Union/Ukraine"), attribution follows
    the secondary listing for post-1991 country names. No "Soviet Union" row exists; SU
    medals attributed to Russia (Novikov, Margulis) or Ukraine (Drinfeld).

    Three documented risks:
    1. Domain slip from user's preferred Education/Higher Education NEW → Science/Mathematics.
       Reason: Wikipedia source coverage was thin for Education comparative seeds (no Top 100
       university table, no tertiary GER table). Comparative 0/5 gap fill prioritized over
       Education 0/16 gap fill. Documented in decision_log R3.
    2. Yau ('82) attributed to Hong Kong (Fields Medal article first-listed); China-mainland
       reattribution would be defensible. Documented in decision_log item 4.
    3. Threshold ">5" yields heavily skewed 4 Yes / 15 No distribution; preserved seed-faithful.

    Creator preflight: 48/48 OK including PK uniqueness, schema consistency, total-medalists
    match (64), Yes/No partition correctness, sort order, claim_type recorded.

    Domain diversity: Science/Mathematics adds depth to existing Science family (3 → 4

Counts by severity: BLOCKING=2 / NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE=0 / SUGGESTION=1
Counts by issue type: factual=0 / structural=2 / scope-related=1

What passes:
- Local table mechanics: 19 rows x 4 columns; CSV header matches draft.columns; column_types cover exactly the four columns; source_count=7 equals len(source_urls); duplicate count for primary_key=(Country) is 0.
- Aggregation arithmetic is internally consistent: Fields Medalists sums to 64; Qualifies (>5) is correct for every staged count; sort order is descending by count with alphabetical tie breaks.
- Category and domain are plausible: comparative as the primary category and aggregation as secondary match the derived threshold column; operation_type=aggregation is reasonable; Science/Mathematics fits the domain taxonomy.
- The master Fields Medal source supports the total medalist count and the 1936-2022 cutoff: it says 64 people had been awarded the medal as of 2022 and that the 2022 group received awards on 5 July 2022 (staged ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fields_Medal, lead, lines 212-213). It also supports that the 2026 awarding is future/planned (same source, list intro, line 225).

Findings:

1. (structural, BLOCKING) The load-bearing source is an affiliation table, not a nationality / country-produced table.

The staged curation repeatedly says the Fields Medal article lists medalists with “primary nationality” and that counts are extracted from a per-medalist nationality line. The cited source does not do that. Its table headers are “Affiliation (when awarded)” and “Affiliation (current/last),” not nationality or country of origin (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fields_Medal, List of Fields medalists table header, lines 226-228). Sample rows confirm the mismatch: Pierre Deligne is listed with IHÉS, France at award and IAS, US current/last, not Belgium (same source, line 254); Shing-Tung Yau is listed with IAS, US and Tsinghua, China, not Hong Kong/China (line 262); Vladimir Drinfeld is listed with a USSR affiliation and University of Chicago, US, not Soviet Union/Ukraine (line 266); Vaughan Jones is listed with US affiliations, not New Zealand (lines 267-268).

This means the source plan does not support the staged Country values or per-country medalist counts under the stated “countries produced” / nationality-style rule. The table may be internally coherent as a manually curated nationality aggregation, but it is not source_defined from the cited master article.

Minimal repair: choose one grounding path and make the artifacts match it. Either (a) retitle/rebuild around affiliation-at-award/current affiliation using the Fields Medal table, or (b) keep the “countries produced” nationality framing but add load-bearing sources for nationality/country attribution for every medalist, not just six validation cases. If using Wikidata, document the property and query snapshot; if using per-medalist Wikipedia pages, source_urls/source_count and Roles need to cover all rows needed for the aggregation.

2. (scope-related, BLOCKING) The 19-country row universe and counts are not recoverable from the cited seven-source set.

Only six per-medalist pages are cited, but the staged counts require assigning all 64 medalists to exactly one country. The master article gives the medalist list and affiliation data, while the six extra pages validate only selected edge cases. They do not support the full country universe or totals such as Belgium=2, Australia=2, New Zealand=1, Norway=1, Vietnam=1, etc. Local locators: datasets/pkdb_bench/staging/countries_with_more_than_5_fields_medalists.csv lines 2-20; draft.json source_urls lines 28-35; curation.json source_coverage_notes Roles block.

This is not a small missing-value issue because the country aggregation is the benchmark’s load-bearing fact. A model could answer using country of birth, citizenship, institutional affiliation at award, current affiliation, or first-listed source convention and produce different country totals. The current title says “countries that have produced,” but the cited source set does not define that country attribution relation across the full medalist universe.

Minimal repair: add a source-defined country-attribution relation for the full universe. Good repair options are a Wikidata/SPARQL construction over Fields Medal award recipients plus an explicit property such as country of citizenship or place of birth; a full set of per-medalist Wikipedia pages if the chosen relation is nationality/citizenship; or a rebuild to affiliation-at-award countries using the already-cited Fields Medal table.

3. (structural, SUGGESTION) The current row design is broader than the seed phrasing, but the title handles this adequately.

The handoff frames the seed as “Which countries have produced more than 5 Fields Medal winners?”, which would naturally return only the four qualifying countries. The staged table instead lists all countries with at least one medalist and includes a Qualifies (>5) column. This is acceptable because the table_title says exactly that, and it gives the comparative column useful negative examples. No fix required; just preserve this broader all-candidate framing in any repair so the CSV shape remains honest.

Final judgment: Not ready. The CSV is mechanically clean, but the core aggregation is not source-grounded by the cited Wikipedia sources because affiliation and nationality/country-produced are being conflated.

Minimal fixes needed:
1. Decide whether Country means affiliation-at-award/current affiliation, nationality/citizenship, place of birth, or another explicit country relation.
2. Rebuild counts from sources that actually expose that relation for all 64 medalists.
3. Update table_title, db_analog, claim_type, temporal_note, source_coverage_notes, and normalization_decisions to match the chosen relation.
4. Append audit_response.cycle_1 and rerun preflight, including a check that the rebuilt country counts sum to 64 under the chosen counting rule.
